faq.q: Can I control which pages from each file get merged, and in what order?
faq.a: Yes. Each added PDF shows a page-range box — leave it blank for all pages, or type something like 1-3,5 to take only those pages from that file. Drag the cards or use the up/down arrows to set the sequence, and an Output-order dropdown offers Keep current, Reverse, and sort by name A→Z or Z→A. The files merge in the order shown on screen.

faq.q: Is there a file count or size limit?
faq.a: There's no hard limit on the number of files, and you need at least two for the Merge button to activate. It warns when the combined size exceeds 50 MB, because browser-based merging can get slow or run out of memory on very large sets. It also validates each page range as you type, telling you if a number exceeds that file's page count.

faq.q: What happens if a PDF is password-protected or corrupt?
faq.a: That file is skipped rather than aborting the whole batch. It's flagged with a reason — "password protected" or "could not be read" — and the readable files still get added and show a page-1 thumbnail. You can add more files at any time or clear everything and start over.

No. Merging runs entirely in your browser using pdf-lib, with pdf.js generating the thumbnails; your PDFs never leave your device. The only thing remembered between visits is your chosen output-order preset, stored locally under pdfMergerOrder. There's also a "Copy merge order" button that copies a text manifest of the files, their order and page counts.
